newsitem.title: UK: Clarke cuts UK standard rate income tax by one pct.
newsitem.headline: Clarke cuts UK standard rate income tax by one pct.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said Britain would cut the standard rate of income tax to 23 percent from 24 percent.
Clarke said the governments control of public spending and borrowing would have allowed him to cut the rate by two percent if he had chosen to.
"But I preferred instead to raise the personal allowances and widen the 20p band for those at the bottom of the scale.
Clarkes said in his budget speech that the basic rate of income tax is now 10 percent lower than the rate the ruling Conservatives inherited in 1979.
"Another penny off the basic rate is a significant further step towards this Government's target of a 20 pence basic rate of tax," Clarke added.
